meta.title: Three.js Game Specification Forge
meta.subtitle: Decide the game in small, understandable steps. Finish with a canonical specification, dependency preflight, and budget-governed Gauntlet Loop handoff.

steps.title: Intake & North Star
steps.eyebrow: 1 · Establish the starting point and promise
steps.description: Classify the workspace, then lock what the game is, who it serves, and what this run is supposed to ship. Architecture stays open until the constraints demand it.

fields.label: Workspace mode
options: Lead agent may create a throwaway prototype first

fields.label: Repository name, URL, or local path
fields.placeholder: my-game or C:\path\to\repo or https://github.com/...

fields.label: Known baseline artifacts and constraints
fields.placeholder: For existing work: code, docs, assets, prior decisions, fixed integrations, and evidence already available. For greenfield: write None — greenfield and list any external constraints.

fields.label: Working title
fields.placeholder: Neon Salvage

fields.label: One-sentence player promise
fields.placeholder: A tense 10-minute browser stealth game where every light is both cover and a weapon.
fields.help: Describe the player's experience, not the technology.

fields.label: Genre and subgenre
fields.placeholder: Isometric extraction action RPG

fields.label: Target player
fields.placeholder: Players who like Hades combat and short, replayable runs

fields.label: What must this implementation run deliver?
fields.placeholder: A polished vertical slice: title screen, tutorialized first run, one complete level, three enemies, one boss, progression summary.

fields.label: Explicit non-goals
fields.placeholder: No accounts, online multiplayer, monetization, procedural campaign, or external backend in this slice.

steps.title: Quality Bar
steps.description: Give critics real references and measurable comparisons. A hard bar supplies direction even when it is not realistically reachable.

fields.label: Inspectable reference URLs — one per line
fields.placeholder:
https://...
https://...
fields.help: Gameplay videos, screenshots, playable games, audio, UX references, or benchmark repos.

fields.label: Visual comparison bar
fields.placeholder: At fixed hero views, our lighting, materials, silhouettes, and scene density should compare favorably side by side with the supplied reference captures.

fields.label: Gameplay comparison bar
fields.placeholder: A fresh player can understand the objective, move, fight, fail, retry, and finish one run without instructions outside the game.

fields.label: Technical and performance bar
fields.placeholder: Sustained 60 FPS at 1080p on the named target device, no console errors, deterministic replay for the same seed.

fields.label: One-sentence strongest bar
fields.placeholder: Our fixed-view captures and first five minutes of play must win blind A/B comparisons against [reference], while meeting the performance gate.

steps.title: Player Experience
steps.eyebrow: 3 · What the player does and feels
steps.description: Define the verbs, controls, viewpoint, onboarding, and accessibility contract before content multiplies.

fields.label: Primary player verbs
fields.placeholder: Move, aim, dash, strike, parry, interact. Explain what makes each skillful.

fields.label: Target feeling
fields.placeholder: Fast, readable, dangerous, empowering after mastery

fields.label: Desktop/gamepad control contract
fields.placeholder: WASD move; mouse aim; LMB attack; Space dodge; remappable keyboard and gamepad parity.

fields.label: Touch control contract
fields.placeholder: Required when mobile/tablet is targeted. Define stick, actions, target selection, orientation.

fields.label: First 90 seconds
fields.placeholder: What the player sees, learns, does, and succeeds at — in order.

steps.title: Core Loop & Rules
steps.description: Lock the smallest complete loop, its pressure, rewards, failure, retry, and skill expression.

fields.label: Moment-to-moment loop
fields.placeholder: Scout → choose route → engage/evade → collect resource → reach safety → upgrade → repeat.

fields.label: Primary objective
fields.placeholder: What does the player need to accomplish, and how is progress visible?

fields.label: Pressure and stakes
fields.placeholder: Enemies, time, resource attrition, escalating alert, shrinking space, score chase.

fields.label: Immediate and long-term rewards
fields.placeholder: Immediate feedback, score, unlocks, new options, mastery, narrative information.

fields.label: Win, fail, and retry rules
fields.placeholder: Exact success/failure conditions, what persists, restart time target, and anti-frustration rules.

fields.label: Difficulty and fairness contract
fields.placeholder: Telegraph times, recovery windows, scaling rules, adaptive difficulty policy, forbidden cheap failures.

fields.label: Where mastery comes from
fields.placeholder: Timing, aiming, route knowledge, planning, resource tradeoffs, execution, team coordination.

steps.title: World & Content Slice
steps.eyebrow: 5 · Enough content to prove the promise
steps.description: Specify the first complete slice and its content inventory. Avoid designing a hundred levels before one is fun.

fields.label: Setting, fantasy, and tone
fields.placeholder: Place, era, player role, conflict, emotional tone, and what makes this world recognizable.

fields.label: First playable slice — beginning to end
fields.placeholder: List the sequence of beats from launch through completion and retry.

fields.label: Required content inventory
fields.placeholder: 1 level; 1 player actor; 3 enemy roles; 2 weapons; 4 pickups; 1 boss; 6 VFX families; title/pause/result screens.

fields.label: Encounter and pacing plan
fields.placeholder: Start, first decision, first threat, first reward, escalation, recovery beat, climax, recap.

fields.label: What must be data-driven
fields.placeholder: Enemy definitions, weapons, encounters, level anchors, rewards, tuning values, localization strings.

steps.title: Systems & State
steps.description: Choose the systems the game truly needs, then define authority, persistence, and data boundaries for the selected slice.

fields.label: Combat / interaction authority
fields.placeholder: Action phases, collision/contact authority, damage rules, invulnerability, interruption, feedback ordering.

fields.label: Enemy / NPC behavior contract
fields.placeholder: Observable inputs, legal intents, state transitions, navigation, spacing, telegraphs, deterministic test fixtures.

fields.label: Progression and economy contract
fields.placeholder: What changes within a run vs across runs; currencies, sources, sinks, unlock rules, caps, reset rules.

fields.label: Save and recovery contract
fields.placeholder: What persists, when it commits, versioning/migration, corruption fallback, offline/local/server authority.

fields.label: Networking and authority contract
fields.placeholder: Server authority, room size, tick rate, prediction/reconciliation, reconnect, anti-cheat boundary.

fields.label: Authored definitions vs runtime state
fields.placeholder: Immutable content IDs/stats/moves live in definitions; transforms/health/cooldowns/current action live in runtime instances.

steps.title: Visual, Camera, UI & Audio
steps.description: Turn taste into inspectable constraints: fixed views, material behavior, readable effects, audio roles, and complete interface states.

fields.label: Art direction in concrete terms
fields.placeholder: Shape language, material identity, texture density, palette, contrast, reference traits to match, traits to avoid.

fields.label: Camera behavior
fields.placeholder: Lens/FOV or orthographic scale, follow lag, framing targets, look limits, collision/occlusion, shake and reduced-motion behavior.

fields.label: Lighting, atmosphere, and weather
fields.placeholder: Key/fill/environment logic, shadow priority, fog model, time/weather transitions, readability constraints.

fields.label: VFX readability contract
fields.placeholder: Telegraphs, attacks, impacts, statuses, trails, residue, quality tiers, reduced-motion alternatives.

fields.label: Audio and music contract
fields.placeholder: Action confirmation, ambience, music states, priority/ducking, spatial audio, UI sounds, mobile unlock, mute controls.

fields.label: Required UI states
fields.placeholder: Loading, title, gameplay HUD, pause, settings, tutorial, fail/retry, win/recap, touch controls, error/recovery.

steps.title: Three.js Technical Contract
steps.description: Lock runtime, device, simulation, performance, and deployment requirements. Leave exact module boundaries to the lead agent unless they are product constraints.

fields.label: Three.js implementation mode
options: Lead agent chooses plain Three.js or R3F

fields.label: Browser/device matrix
fields.placeholder: Current Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Safari; target desktop GPU/CPU; named Android/iPhone baseline; orientation.

fields.label: Performance and memory budget
fields.placeholder: 60 FPS desktop / 30 or 60 mobile; max DPR; draw-call/triangle/texture/bundle targets; loading-time target.

fields.label: Simulation and determinism
options: Real-time only; deterministic replay not required

fields.label: Physics / collision expectation
options: Simple authored collision; no full engine

fields.label: Build and deployment target
fields.placeholder: Vite production build on GitHub Pages/Cloudflare/Vercel; base path; HTTPS; asset CDN; backend if any.

fields.label: Security, privacy, and secret boundaries
fields.placeholder: No secrets client-side; external API calls behind server routes; telemetry consent; content security; save-data policy.

steps.title: Assets & Dependency Strategy
steps.description: Choose how assets may be created, what licensing is acceptable, and which resources the preflight should inspect before implementation.

fields.label: License and provenance policy
options: Any commercial-compatible license with attribution manifest

fields.label: Hero assets requiring individual quality loops
fields.placeholder: Player body/hands, signature weapon, main enemy, boss, hero environment, sky, UI identity, signature sound.

fields.label: Asset delivery budgets
fields.placeholder: Per-model triangle/texture/animation limits, total compressed payload, LOD policy, KTX2/Meshopt/Draco policy.

fields.label: External services/API policy
fields.placeholder: Which generation APIs/MCPs are allowed; keys supplied through environment only; fallback when unavailable.

fields.label: Dependency constraints
fields.placeholder: Prefer maintained packages; pin versions; no client secrets; justify every dependency; preserve existing stack in existing repos.

fields.label: Feasibility risks, required spikes, and deferred non-blockers
fields.placeholder: For each high-risk assumption: evidence or spike plan, owner, and decision trigger. List deferred non-blockers with owner/trigger. Write None with rationale only when no material risks or deferrals remain.

steps.title: Acceptance & Evidence
steps.description: Specify what must be exercised in the real browser. Builders report evidence; critics inspect artifacts, not summaries.

fields.label: Primary browser journey
fields.placeholder: Launch → start → learn → complete representative interaction/encounter → pause/resume → fail/retry → win/recap.

fields.label: Acceptance criteria — one check per line
fields.placeholder:
A new player completes the slice without external instructions.
Same input + seed produces identical simulation trace.
No console errors in production preview.

fields.label: Fixed evidence captures
fields.placeholder: Named screenshots/views, video segments, profiler traces, browser/device runs, audio captures, comparison grid format.

fields.label: Release-blocking failures
fields.placeholder: Broken primary journey, console errors, missing assets, secrets in client bundle, inaccessible controls, budget regressions, unlicensed content.

fields.label: Definition of done
fields.placeholder: The deployed exact commit passes all gates, critics approve each important piece against the bar, and known limitations are documented.

steps.title: Gauntlet Run Limits
steps.eyebrow: 11 · Bound the machine before it starts
steps.description: The loop remains open-ended in rounds, but must stop before crossing the first measurable time, spend, or token ceiling. Reserve capacity for integration and final verification.

fields.label: Token ceiling in millions (0 = unavailable/not enforced)
What the spend ceiling includes
options: All lead + subagent model usage; paid APIs require separate approval
Model usage and paid generation APIs combined
Harness-reported model spend only; track other costs separately

fields.label: How limits are enforced
options: Launcher / gateway hard-enforces every supported ceiling
Prompt-only best effort — no hard enforcement

fields.label: Reserve for integration and final QA (%)
If evidence shows a quality plateau
options: Stop when no feasible evidence-backed improvement remains
Pause for approval with the best next experiment
Continue until another mandatory stop condition occurs

fields.label: When exact spend/token telemetry is unavailable
options: Enforce wall time + concurrency; report estimates
Require harness telemetry or stop before work

steps.title: Handoff & Launch Contract
steps.eyebrow: 12 · Freeze canon, then give the agent room
steps.description: Name the workspace and delivery rules. The exported directive stays short; the attached specification carries the decisions.

fields.label: Package manager
options: Lead agent decides for new repo

fields.label: Git delivery rule
fields.placeholder: Work on a feature branch/worktree, use reviewable commits, never push directly to the protected default branch, report the final commit and deployment URL.

fields.label: Human approval gates
fields.placeholder: Approval required before paid API use, public publishing, destructive migrations, or raising a run limit.

fields.label: Known open questions the lead may resolve
fields.placeholder: Only list decisions intentionally delegated. Blank means the spec is expected to be closed.

fields.label: Final constraints or context
fields.placeholder: Existing docs, required integrations, legal constraints, links, environment notes.

resources.role: App/game state outside transient scene objects

resources.name: Visual Asset Browser
resources.role: Curated asset sourcing with license filters

resources.name: GameBlocks
resources.role: Known-good coordinate, motion, camera, and world modules
